a.question: How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?
a.observed_answer:
1. Remove Personal and Corporate Objective cards showing a player count above four; shuffle each deck separately and deal each player one of each face down.
2. At the first Encounter, each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives; remove the other face down, unseen by anyone.
3. No. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger the First Encounter choice.

Draw to 5 at the start of the Player Phase; when a required Action draw finds the deck empty, shuffle that Character's Action discard into a new deck. Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this. a.question: You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?
reader_requested_parts: Cost-2 Action card payment from stated hand
a.observed_answer:
1. Discard the played Action card plus two additional Action cards (three Action cards total); the two Contamination cards cannot pay. The stated hand has only two other Action cards, so it cannot pay the full cost.
2. No. Contamination cards are not Action cards and can never pay an Action cost.
3. Choose one of the card’s OR sections.
a.reader_evidence:
1. **Action Cost:** each Action's icon shows a number — discard exactly that many Action cards from your hand (face up) to pay. **For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.** Basic, Room and Item Actions have no played Action card to add to their printed cost; pay any separate Ammo, Item-component or other requirements as instructed. **Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.** Each Character has a partially unique deck of 10 Action cards. To use one, discard that card face up **and** pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one.
2. **Action Cost:** each Action's icon shows a number — discard exactly that many Action cards from your hand (face up) to pay. **For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.** Basic, Room and Item Actions have no played Action card to add to their printed cost; pay any separate Ammo, Item-component or other requirements as instructed. **Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.** - Contamination cards can never pay costs.
3. Each Character has a partially unique deck of 10 Action cards. To use one, discard that card face up **and** pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one. The original manual illustrates these card effects on page 13:
a.expected_answer: Discard the played card and two additional Action cards face up. Contamination cannot pay costs. Choose one OR effect.
a.reason: The stated hand contains exactly the played card plus the two additional Action cards required. The explicit assertion that it cannot pay the full cost is materially false, even though the preceding cost statement and evidence are correct.

a.question: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
a.observed_answer:
1. Use corresponding Evacuation Section Room Action: cost 2 cards, Pod unlocked with free character space, section free of Intruder and Malfunction. Roll Noise first; Intruder present/appearing/reaching Section makes boarding fail.
2. Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. On boarding you may launch immediately or wait (pass this turn; remain present for bag-development Noise rolls). At start of first round in each later Player Phase, choose remain and pass, launch, or exit free to Section Room and take full 2-Action round.
3. May still wait, launch or exit; Malfunction prevents only new entry. A second Character boarding a waiting Pod may launch both immediately.
a.reader_evidence:
1. - **Board:** pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. - **Hibernatorium** — Try to hibernate: pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing in the Room makes the attempt fail. Otherwise remove your miniature and stop participating until the end checks. **Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception.** A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.
2. - **At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase**, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2). - **Wait after boarding:** you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1).
3. - **A Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait:** you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods (FAQ Rules 3). - **A second Character boards your waiting Pod:** the **new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants aboard**. Waiting by the first occupant does not prevent this launch or reserve launch control for them.
a.expected_answer: Use corresponding Evacuation Room Action cost 2, unlocked Pod with free space, no Intruder/Malfunction. Roll Noise first and fail if Intruder reaches Room. Two Character spaces; Heavy Objects use none. Enter then launch immediately or wait and pass current turn. At start of first round next Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or free exit followed by a full two-Action round. Intruder appearing in Section returns all Pod occupants; another boarder may immediately launch.
a.reason: The requested consequences of waiting omit the compulsory return of all Pod occupants in the Section to its Room when an Intruder appears there. Answer, checklist and cited factual evidence do not supply that consequence; the rest is correct.

a.question: How are the basic and additional Room tiles and Exploration tokens placed at setup; what Coordinates, Destination, Time, Engines, Eggs and Weaknesses start on the board?
a.observed_answer:
1. Shuffle tiles 2 unseen and place one face-down per “2” slot, return excess unseen; place all tiles 1 on “1” slots. Shuffle Exploration tokens unseen, one face-down per Room tile; return excess.
2. Place one random Coordinates card face-down by Cockpit; Destination marker on B track space; Time marker on green Time Track space.
3. For each Engine shuffle one Working and one Damaged token face-down and stack on slot, top is true status. Place 5 Eggs and 3 random Weakness cards face-down in slots.
a.reader_evidence:
1. 4. Shuffle the Exploration tokens (unseen) and place one face down on each Room tile. Return the rest to the box. 2. Shuffle all Room tiles "2" without looking at their fronts and randomly place one face down on each Room slot marked "2". Return the rest to the box unseen (there are more tiles than slots — players never know exactly which Rooms are on the ship).
2. 5. Place 1 random Coordinates card face down on its space next to the Cockpit. Return the rest to the box. - **Cockpit** — Check Coordinates (secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie; replace it and remember it) OR Set Destination (move the Destination marker). **The marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card:** read the entry corresponding to its track space when checking where the ship will jump. You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating.
3. 8. For each Engine (1, 2, 3): take its two Engine tokens (1 Damaged, 1 Working), shuffle them face down, and stack them face down on the matching Engine slot. **The top token indicates the true status of that Engine.** Players must not see the token fronts. 9. Place the Intruder board next to the board with **5 Egg tokens** and **3 random Weakness cards face down** in their slots. Return remaining Weakness cards to the box.
a.expected_answer: All 11 basic tiles face down in 1 slots; five random additional tiles face down in 2 slots, leftovers boxed unseen; random face-down Exploration per tile. Random face-down Coordinates, Destination B, Time green. Each numbered Engine has shuffled Damaged/Working pair face down, top true status. Five Eggs, three random face-down Weaknesses.
a.reason: The requested basic-Room setup specifies placing all tiles 1 in slots 1 but never states that those Room tiles are face down. The same-question evidence gives face-down additional tiles and Exploration tokens only, not the omitted basic-tile concealment rule. Other setup parts match.

b.question: When are Action hands refilled and the First Player token passed; what happens when the Action deck empties, and what are the normal discard destinations and visibility?
b.observed_answer: 1) At Player Phase start everyone draws to five (six with Cabins). 2) After drawing, pass First Player token left except first game turn. 3) When deck empty for required draw, shuffle discard into a new deck and draw. 4) Normal card discards are face up; Action and gained Contamination go to own Action discard, Items to matching discard, Event/Attack/Serious Wound to respective piles. Explicit exceptions: search rejected card face down bottom of deck.
b.reader_evidence: [1] Every player draws from their Action deck up to a hand of 5 cards; Cabins gives a hand of 6. [2] After drawing, pass First Player token to the player on the left; do not pass it on the first turn. [3] Whenever you must draw and your Action deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck, then draw. [4] Normal card discards are face up; Action and gained Contamination cards go to that Character's Action discard pile; Items to matching Item discard; Event, Intruder Attack and Serious Wound cards to their own discard piles. Search/Storage return rejected card face down to bottom of chosen deck.
b.expected_answer: At Player Phase start draw to 5, shuffle Action discard whenever required draw finds empty deck; then pass token left except first turn. Actions/Contamination to own Action discard, Items/Event/Attack/Serious Wounds to respective discard piles face up; markers to pools. Search example has explicit face-down return exception.
b.reason: The broadly asked normal discard destinations are incomplete: the answer/evidence supplies card destinations and visibility but never states where discarded markers go. This is an omission, not a false affirmative ruling.

assessment: A false fixed-four Objective filter carries an unprovided premise across questions; A payment conclusion contradicts correct three-card calculation; A omits forced Pod exit and basic-Room face-down placement. B omits normal marker destination. All are actual requested known-source facts, not automatic source-gap or confidence deductions.
